edges.description: The substituted side chain bonds directly to the heme iron, holding it in the oxidized ferric state.
In distal (E7) variants the ferric lock co-occurs with stabilization of the deoxy quaternary state.
In proximal (F8) variants the ferric lock co-occurs with an unstable, high-affinity tetramer.
The structurally stabilized ferric heme resists enzymatic and pharmacologic reduction.
The distal class contributes a persistent methemoglobin fraction with lowered whole-tetramer oxygen affinity.

nodes.description: The mutant beta subunit is locked with its heme iron in the ferric (Fe3+) state, i.e. as methemoglobin, which cannot reversibly bind oxygen. From this shared lesion the beta variants branch by which heme-contact residue is affected, and the ferric lock is also resistant to the normal reductive pathway.

nodes.description: A heterozygous germline HBB missense variant substitutes a residue that coordinates the heme iron of the beta-globin chain -- most commonly the distal (E7) or proximal (F8) histidine, replaced by tyrosine, or the E11 valine replaced by glutamate. The introduced side chain forms a direct bond to the heme iron. This is a neomorphic, dominant structural change rather than loss of function.

evidence.snippet: These amino acid substitutions in the heme binding pocket cause structural alterations which stabilize the ferric state, resulting in extremely low oxygen affinity and resistance to reduction.
Hemoglobin M variants have altered function, suggesting a neomorphic mechanism of pathogenicity, due to increased stabilization of the ferric state.

genetic_context.description: Heterozygous germline missense variant in a heme-contact residue of beta-globin, recorded as NEOMORPHIC because the mutant chain still assembles into hemoglobin but confers a novel deleterious property -- stabilization of the ferric heme state -- absent from wild-type.

nodes.description: beta92(F8) His>Tyr (codon 92 CAC>TAC), the proximal histidine; also known as Hb M-Akita and Hb M-Milwaukee-2. Yields an unstable hemoglobin with raised oxygen affinity, loss of cooperativity, and mild hemolysis.

This is the key mechanistic distinction from the enzymatic (CYB5R3) and acquired forms of methemoglobinemia, in which methylene blue is effective.
